name: Eastern Lowlands (Santa Cruz · Chaco · Amazon Basin)

language.script_notes: Spanish signage; Guaraní is spoken in the southeast and other lowland Indigenous languages in the north. Cruceño Spanish and a less Andean cultural feel than the highlands.

road_furniture.bollard_color: Red-and-white bollards on some routes, such as the north-south RN9.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: As national; far less needed on flat roads.
road_furniture.line_paint: Orange center lines on some north-south routes.
road_furniture.curb_style: Wide, planned ring roads in Santa Cruz; dirt roads in rural areas.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Thick lumber utility poles as national; the RN4 near Santa Cruz has distinctive paving through flat, green terrain.

architecture.roof_style: Low-pitched or flat roofs of corrugated metal and concrete; roofs with wide overhangs against sun and rain.
architecture.wall_construction: Cement-painted house walls are common at low altitude; colonial-era white-walled mission towns in the Chiquitania with carved wooden Jesuit churches; modern high-rise development in Santa Cruz.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Painted cement in warm colours, and white colonial walls.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Jesuit mission churches in wood and adobe in the Chiquitania; Santa Cruz's modern skyline and ring roads; ranch buildings across the lowland plains.

nature.vegetation: Flat, green and extensively forested — dry tropical forest in the Chiquitania, dense rainforest in the north, thorny scrub in the southern Chaco, and large soy and sugar cane farms around the main city.
nature.terrain: Flat lowlands from the foot of the Andes to the Amazon basin and Chaco plain, at only a few hundred metres above sea level — Santa Cruz sits at 416m.
nature.climate_signature: Hot, humid and green, with a wet season — a complete contrast to the cold, treeless highlands.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Mototaxis and motorcycles are far more common than in the highlands; pickups on farms and ranches.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Concentrated on Santa Cruz and the main highways; big gaps in the Chaco and the northern Amazon.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Chaco plain and flat green farmland
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Paraguayan plates and road furniture differ, and signage there has Guaraní alongside Spanish more widely; thick lumber poles and the white-backed Street View car point here.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Amazon-edge farmland and rainforest along the border
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Portuguese signage and Brazilian yellow centre lines and Mercosul plates differ from Spanish signage here.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same national road furniture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The east is flat, green and hot; the west is high, cold and treeless.
